instructions: Count drift (owner fix 8). Where: the resin vote and the plank. What's wrong: the chapter says 'Forty-two odiyans' and 'divided the cup into forty-two', but then shows 'forty-one names' on the plank after Neela adds hers, and everyone still says 'the forty'. Change: make the plank hold forty-two names once Neela chalks hers last. Keep the cup at forty-two.

Count drift, continued. Where: the first natural use of 'the forty' after the count. Change: add one short line saying 'the forty' is the name they kept after the number stopped being true. Keep it to a single sentence, in Neela's voice, and make it lightly wry rather than expository.

'Flat' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: every 'flat' used for a voice or delivery in this chapter, such as 'His voice was flat' or 'said it flatly'. What's wrong: 'flat' is the default delivery word across the book. Change: from now on, 'flat' belongs only to Usha's voice, at most once per chapter. Replace every other use here with a specific action beat or a specific quality of delivery. Examples: he reads the sails off like a tally; he doesn't raise his voice; a pause before the number. If Usha speaks at the dusk arrival and the word fits her, one use may stay.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter the vote scene. Devan asks the Company for leave and never looks at Neela, he waits for the hands, and her hand goes up last. Do not alter the reveal of the sixty sails, with Neela counting them and knowing the curve of Nellimala beach. Keep the stated ages: Neela twenty-seven, Devan thirty-two.

Ending explains what the scene showed (owner fix 4). Where: the chapter close. What's wrong: 'It was the truth. It was the only kind of answer he had ever given her, and she took it, as she always did.' summarises a beat the reader already felt. Change: cut those sentences. End on Devan's 'I can't tell,' and then her cold hand in his. Add no summary or interior gloss after the hand.

'Flat' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: every voice or delivery 'flat' in Devan's POV, including any 'flat green case'. Change: keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once in the chapter. Replace the others with specifics. Describe the case concretely, for example 'the green writing case' or its lacquer or clasp, not 'flat'.

Writ continuity (owner fix 2). Leave the ch 2 writ beats as written: Devan carried the writ up the hill rather than leave it in the hollow behind the third slat, and he checks the oilcloth in his pack. Ch 21 will put it back in the hollow, so ch 30 stays true.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter Neela's line to Usha, 'Nicked his chin shaving three days back and I found out over my rice.' Do not alter Devan's POV turning that line into a lever the queen now holds.

Count consistency, following from the ch 1 change to forty-two (owner fix 8). Where: the descent, and any other place the narration states a literal headcount, such as 'forty odiyans' on the ropes. Change: wherever 'forty' is meant as an exact count, make it 'forty-two' or rephrase as 'the forty' used as the Company's name. Leave 'the forty' as the name untouched.

Staging slip 1 (owner fix 7). Where: 'He would be at the cistern shed now, or on a wall.' What's wrong: Devan is at the shelf in the lower narrows at this point (ch 14 and 17). Change: place him at the shelf in the lower narrows, for example 'He would be on the shelf now, counting arrows he didn't need'. Keep the line's function: she can't reach him.

Staging slip 2 (owner fix 7). Where: 'You climbed in by the spray slot.' What's wrong: ch 15 has Neela climbing the sea stair by rope from the cliff foot, and ch 15 never shows a spray slot. Change: rewrite the queen's line to match ch 15, for example 'You came up the sea stair on a rope at the noon gun.' Do not add a spray slot to ch 15.

Staging slip 3 (owner fix 7). Where: 'the fading ache where a hook had not been'. What's wrong: it reads as a typo, because the hook did land: Devan's hook welt tore across her ribs in ch 15. Change: rewrite to 'the fading ache where the hook had been', or name it concretely, for example 'the hook-welt along her ribs, fading'.

'Flat' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: 'Her flat voice cracked' and any other voice 'flat' in the chapter. Change: if the speaker is Usha, one use may stay. Otherwise, and for every additional use, replace it with a specific beat. The queen's register should be kind and dangerous at once, so render it through what she does with the pen or the lamp, not through 'flat'.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter 'You carried away paper. You can't carry away what I saw.' Do not alter the snap-together of Chathu's rat-eaten page and Kamalakshi's question, Neela leaving her thumb unpricked so the queen can't see the lever, or the reveal that the queen spent her whole noon on the crate.

Writ location (owner fix 2). Where: the dawn beat when Neela opens the hollow in the shutter frame. What's wrong: ch 2 established that Devan carried the payment writ up the hill in his pack, so it can't 'still be there' in the hollow. Change: the hollow holds the chit and the gift seal. Devan takes the oilcloth with the writ from his pack and puts it back in the hollow behind the third slat while she watches. One or two concrete sentences are enough. Keep his line that he will read the writ aloud before the queen. This makes ch 30's 'lifted it out of the hollow behind the third slat at dawn' true.
Protect. Do not change the explicit scene or its new term: the lamp kept lit, being seen as a choice, and the refusal split between them, hers to speak and his to stand behind.

'Good hand' and 'flat' check (owner fix 6, pattern). Where: after the spear takes his right hand. Change: if the text starts calling his left 'his good hand' or 'the good one', replace it with 'his left' or with the gesture itself. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.
'Good hand' and 'flat' check (owner fix 6, pattern). Change: replace any 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the action. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.
'Good hand' and 'flat' check (owner fix 6, pattern). Change: replace any 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the action. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.

Loose pages from ch 24 (owner fix 8). Where: the morning roll-signing in the lower court, before or just after Neela writes her name. What's wrong: Neela promised in ch 24 to hand back the eleven Resin House pages at first light, and the book never shows it. Change: add one sentence showing her handing the eleven pages back to their owners by daylight, before she signs. It fits the chapter's daylight-witness theme. Do not expand it into a scene.

'Good hand' and 'flat' check (owner fix 6, pattern). Where: the left-handed signature and around it. Change: replace any 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the gesture. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.
'Good hand' and 'flat' check (owner fix 6, pattern). Change: replace any 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the action. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.

The queen dodges the writ (owner fix 5). Where: her answer after Devan reads the payment writ aloud. What's wrong: 'I held that a realm is safe by what it has not seen. It is only blind.' is a thesis, not an admission made to his face. Change: before that thesis, give her one plain line to Devan directly, for example 'I sealed it. Seven weeks before your wedding. I knew what it bought.' Check the interval against earlier books and the bible. If a different interval is established, use that. Then show the hall reacting in a concrete beat or two: Janu, Muthu, the Company, or Usha's welted arm. Keep the thesis line after the hall's reaction. Leave the fuller record to the ch 31 charter clause.

Witness-rule gap (owner fix 1). Where: the dusk self-naming, after Neela narrates Sajan stopping at the edge of the court and not stepping out. What's wrong: Neela then says 'That's all of them,' which is false under the book's witness rule, because the queen could still write Sajan. Change her line to 'That's all who'll come tonight.' Keep Sajan stopping at the edge.

'Flat' and 'good hand' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: throughout. What's wrong: 'his good hand' and 'the good one' recur heavily across ch 30 to 32 (ten or more uses), and 'flat' recurs as a delivery word, for example 'voice... was flat'. Change: replace each 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the gesture alone ('he held the writ out'). Use 'his left' no more than three times in the chapter. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter Madhavi's objection to clause five ('If the crown can hire us to hold a pass, it can hire us to die on one') or Devan amending the clause on the spot. Do not alter Janu's 'Me? I'm sixty-one' and her complaint about the cairn-fire rice. Leave 'lifted it out of the hollow behind the third slat at dawn' as written, since ch 21 now supports it.

Pay off Sajan and close the rule gap (owner fix 1). Where: after the queen burns the crown leaf in the gate fire-basket. Change: Sajan burns his own leaf at the gate basket, then names himself to his brother Sanu there, with Sanu's sleeve touching his. Self-naming needs a dusk turning with the chosen person looking at him (ch 20 rule), so stage it at dusk the same day, at the gate basket, before the tent scene. Keep it to a few lines, with no speech about it. Do not change Sanu's existing bond to Kandan. The share runs both ways, and Sajan naming himself to Sanu is a separate bond.

Cut the false-alarm cliffhanger (owner fix 3). Where: the chapter ending. What's wrong: the chapter ends on the horn ('Lone climber! ...') and 'This is our first vote, Neela.' Ch 32 then deflates it as a barefoot boy with a satchel, and the 'first vote' is spent twice. Change: end the chapter on the sleeve exchange ('Ask.' / 'My sleeve. If you would.'). Cut the horn, the 'Lone climber' call, and the 'first vote' line entirely. Any dawn hitch-counting should sit before the sleeve exchange so the sleeve is the last beat.

Counting repetition (owner fix 6). Where: dialogue that repeats 'counted the road four times' and similar counting tallies. Change: Neela's counting is character and stays, but cut one or two instances in this chapter, starting with the repeated 'counted the road four times'. Do not cut the dawn hitch-count.

'Good hand' and 'flat' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: the charter scene and the explicit scene. Change: replace every 'his good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the action itself. In the explicit scene especially, let her guidance and his asking carry it through gesture. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter Haran's plea to strike the clause, or Neela closing her mouth on 'Keep it.' Do not alter the explicit scene's core. The hand at the nape of her neck, 'the place for wait', becomes only his. The bargain is remade: she is his right hand, and he is the place her vigilance stops. Both leads are adults, as stated in ch 1, and the scene is consensual. Keep both as written.

Remove the deflated climber (owner fix 3). Where: the subordinate clause explaining that the lone climber was a barefoot boy with a satchel. Change: delete it and any other reference back to a horn or climber from ch 31. Let the pepper factors' letter arrive fresh in this chapter, with its own short, concrete arrival beat. This chapter now holds the only 'first vote', so keep 'We vote at noon' as the hinge line.

Narration explains what the scene showed (owner fix 4). Where: the paragraph that begins 'Neela understood why she had asked in the open...' and walks through the diplomatic logic of the lean-vote. Change: cut the paragraph entirely. Go straight from the murmur in the doorway to her nod.

Signposted callback (owner fix 4). Where: the shutter callback 'Once, at the foot of a stair...'. Change: trim it to the image alone, with no 'once' framing and no reminder of where it came from. The reader carries the memory.

Sajan consistency, following ch 31 (owner fix 1). Where: any line or door-roll beat that implies Sajan is still unnamed or that his freedom rests on the charter alone. Change: treat Sajan as self-named to Sanu. If the door roll or hall lists pairs, one brief mention is allowed but not required.

'Good hand' and 'flat' pattern (owner fix 6). Where: the left-handed drill and Muthu's round. Change: replace every 'good hand' or 'the good one' with 'his left' or with the action. The left-handed drill already shows it, so let the moves carry it. Keep 'flat' only for Usha's voice, at most once.

Protect (owner Keep). Do not alter Muthu's left-handed round, where Devan loses and laughs first. Do not alter Ponni at the door board ('That's the girl I carried round the bend'). Keep the hinge: the Thurai envoy and the salt-and-clove-bark rogue odiyan in no ledger.

notes_not_actioned.note: Blurb: 'The closing book of The Odiyan Contracts' fights the ending.
notes_not_actioned.why: This is blurb and metadata, not chapter text, so route it to the blurb and packaging stage. Recommendation: the outline lists this as Book 3, and ch 32 opens series threads (C12, C13, the Thurai hire). Call it 'Book 3' and drop 'closing', which also avoids over-promising under the failure modes.
